stage: before old reviews, programs, readiness, root or sibling mathematical conclusions
literal_target: Smooth closed immersion in R3, continuous osculating planes containing first and second derivatives, continuous injective orthogonal binormal vector field; asks nonzero linking with sufficiently small push-off. Source does not explicitly normalize B, require nonzero B, embed centerline, require B differentiable, regular, rectifiable or curvature nonzero.
independent_reconstruction: For a unit differentiable compatible B and arclength tangent T, N=B cross T gives Tprime=kappa_s N, Nprime=-kappa_s T+tau B, Bprime=-tau N. Twist density (T cross B) dot Bprime equals tau.

For regular spherical B, tau has constant sign. Spherical unit tangent is -sign(tau)N and oriented geodesic curvature equals kappa_s/abs(tau), so the signed geodesic-curvature integral equals integral kappa_s ds.

Jordan Gauss-Bonnet forces absolute signed integral below 2pi, whereas a closed regular space curve with signed curvature never zero has total curvature at least 2pi: this excludes the conjunction of nonvanishing curvature and regular simple spherical binormal.
This argument does not establish nonzero linking because writhe can cancel twist, and it does not apply automatically to merely injective continuous or smooth nonregular spherical B.
Nonunit injectivity and spherical injectivity must be distinguished. Generic radial separation could remove repetitions of directions. That possibility must be tested rather than assumed impossible.
Smooth nonregular spherical binormal test curves with nonzero centerline curvature must be explored; injectivity of a smooth curve alone never certifies nonzero derivative.
falsifiers: Darboux or twist sign inconsistent with orientation reversal, B sign reversal, or nonconstant speed.
A putative Gauss-Bonnet proof using regularity without ensuring Bprime is everywhere nonzero.

A countermodel for literal unnormalized B with disjoint push-off and zero linking; it would invalidate any unqualified equivalence to the unit formulation, not automatically settle the intended normalized problem.
A claimed global conclusion inferred solely from formal algebra or finite numerical samples.
Finite-length or compatibility-preserving approximation assumed without construction.
